task: This is a synthetic exercise using fictional reporting notes. Use only the supplied reporting notes as the fixed record: select, organize and phrase the story without inventing additional reported events, scenes, quotations or reporting activity. Write a headline and a straight news update of roughly 450–650 words in AP style for general newspaper readers about the merger of the East Fen and Lower Rill drainage districts. Write from this reporting snapshot as of September 18, 2026.

facts.text: The fictional county approved a merger of the East Fen and Lower Rill drainage districts, effective Jan. 1, 2027.
The merger creates one administrative board for districts that currently maintain adjoining but separately managed channels and pumping equipment.
East Fen's current operating budget is $230,000 and Lower Rill's is $170,000, totaling $400,000 before transition expenses.
The county has not adopted a final combined budget or forecast a specific reduction in household assessments.
Existing assessment schedules will remain in place for the first year while the new board reviews costs and service boundaries.
The merger does not physically connect every channel or immediately change the equipment serving a particular neighborhood.
A joint maintenance survey found work near the shared boundary was sometimes deferred while the districts clarified responsibility.
The survey records those administrative delays but does not attribute a measured amount of flood damage to them.
County infrastructure director Halen Sore said, "One board can settle a boundary question faster, but the water will still follow the ground we have."
An interim board will include three representatives from each existing district and an independent chair for the transition year.
The supplied merger agreement leaves future permanent representation arrangements for a later county decision.
Maintenance employees will transfer to the combined district without a reduction in posts under the approved transition plan.
A residents group in the lower-lying district asked for published work priorities so its needs remain visible within a larger administration.
Residents group secretary Mera Clove said, "A single letterhead will help only if we can still see which jobs are waiting and why."
The new district will publish a consolidated list of maintenance projects and unresolved responsibility questions.
Emergency reporting numbers will remain active during the transition, with calls routed to the same duty team.
The merger does not replace the county's separate emergency-management responsibilities.
Each district currently uses a different numbering system for channels, which staff will cross-reference rather than erase from old records.
The district offices will initially remain open at both existing locations.
A later decision about office accommodation is not part of the approved merger package.
The transition plan requires an inventory of equipment condition before the board considers shared replacement purchases.
No new pump purchase or guarantee of reduced flooding accompanies the administrative approval.

forbidden_additions: Immediate rate cuts, physical reconnection of channels or guaranteed flood reduction.
Staff reductions, closed offices or approved equipment purchases.
Measured flood losses attributed to the boundary delays.
preserve: Administrative consolidation distinguished from physical works and future funding decisions.
The transition-year arrangements and lower-district representation concern.
Exact quotation wording and attribution when quotations are used.
